---
title: "Reproduce two Bioconductor regressions"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
description: >
  Reuse named tests for a zero-column matrix product and for missing values
  in a sparse matrix conversion from HDF5.
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Reproduce two Bioconductor regressions}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
---

These cases exercise two reported bugs with small, deterministic inputs.
The vignette runs against the installed dependencies, which should pass
both checks. The historical results below were obtained by running the
same generated tests with older upstream revisions. For an introduction
to recording and replaying failures, see the
[sample-alignment walkthrough](replay-walkthrough.html).

## Set up the cases

Use this temporary source tree to try both recipes. In your own package,
put the `@testCases` blocks in the relevant R source files and declare
the test dependencies in `DESCRIPTION`.

```{r setup}
work <- tempfile("bioc-regressions-")
pkg <- file.path(work, "backendregressions")
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "R"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "tests", "testthat"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(pkg, "longtests", "testthat"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c(
  "Package: backendregressions",
  "Version: 0.0.1",
  "Encoding: UTF-8",
  "Suggests: DelayedArray, HDF5Array, Matrix, testthat (>= 3.3.0), withr",
  "Config/testthat/edition: 3"
), file.path(pkg, "DESCRIPTION"))
writeLines(character(), file.path(pkg, "NAMESPACE"))
```

## Keep matrix attributes when the result has zero columns

[DelayedArray #113](https://github.com/Bioconductor/DelayedArray/issues/113)
reported that multiplying an unnamed delayed matrix by a zero-column
matrix returned `list(NULL, NULL)` as its dimension names. Base R returns
`NULL`, which matters when downstream tests compare complete objects.
A 2-by-3 input and a 3-by-0 multiplier reproduce the attribute mismatch,
with a one-column multiplier as a control.

```{r zero-columns}
writeLines(r"(
#' @testCases delayed-matmul
#' list(
#'   cases = list("zero-columns" = list(suite = "tests")),
#'   test = {
#'     x <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2L)
#'     y <- matrix(1:3, ncol = 1L)
#'     delayed <- DelayedArray::DelayedArray(x)
#'     expect_identical(as.matrix(delayed %*% y), x %*% y)
#'     empty <- y[, integer(), drop = FALSE]
#'     expect_identical(as.matrix(delayed %*% empty), x %*% empty)
#'   }
#' )
NULL
)", file.path(pkg, "R", "delayed-matmul.R"))
```

## Preserve `NaN` during sparse coercion

[HDF5Array #61](https://github.com/Bioconductor/HDF5Array/issues/61)
reported that a stored `NaN` survived a delayed operation and then became
zero when coerced to `dgCMatrix`. The fix was in
[DelayedArray](https://github.com/Bioconductor/DelayedArray/commit/1689c0f9f1deb6cff0e64067a37412d4f6d7b330).
The 2-by-2 fixture keeps a nonzero value, two structural zeros and a `NaN`.
The test writes a real TENx HDF5 file, checks the backend and verifies the
value before coercion. The final assertion compares the result to the
expected dense matrix, including the missing value.

```{r sparse-coercion}
writeLines(r"(
#' @testCases tenx-coercion
#' list(
#'   cases = list("preserve-nan" = list(suite = "longtests")),
#'   test = {
#'     counts <- matrix(c(NaN, 0, 0, 2), nrow = 2L)
#'     dir <- withr::local_tempdir()
#'     file <- file.path(dir, "counts.h5")
#'     stored <- HDF5Array::writeTENxMatrix(counts, file, group = "counts")
#'     expect_s4_class(stored, "TENxMatrix")
#'     scaled <- stored * 10
#'     expect_true(is.nan(scaled[1L, 1L]))
#'     converted <- methods::as(scaled, "dgCMatrix")
#'     expect_s4_class(converted, "dgCMatrix")
#'     expect_identical(as.matrix(converted), counts * 10)
#'   }
#' )
NULL
)", file.path(pkg, "R", "tenx-coercion.R"))
```

## Run both regressions

Generate the files and require both case IDs to complete without warnings.
The HDF5 case lives in `longtests` to show how to keep a backend-specific
check in a separate suite. Its fixture here takes little space.

```{r generate, message=FALSE}
invisible(roxygen2::roxygenise(
  pkg, roclets = "biocroxytest::tests_roclet", load_code = roxygen2::load_source
))
ids <- c("delayed-matmul/zero-columns", "tenx-coercion/preserve-nan")
```

```{r current-check}
report <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = ids, seed = 42L)
biocroxytest::check_test_plan(report, required = ids)
report$cases[c("id", "suite", "status")]
```

## Results on historical revisions

Each pair used separate libraries on macOS arm64 with R 4.4.3 and
Bioconductor 3.20 dependencies, including S4Arrays 1.6.0 and SparseArray
1.6.2. Only DelayedArray changed within each pair.
For the HDF5 case, both runs used HDF5Array 1.33.5
([revision `12fae3d`](https://github.com/Bioconductor/HDF5Array/commit/12fae3d2b62c6bb5495fb818efbfde8a8efc6303)).

| Case | DelayedArray revision that failed | Observed mismatch | DelayedArray revision that passed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delayed-matmul/zero-columns` | [0.29.7 (`854795f`)](https://github.com/Bioconductor/DelayedArray/commit/854795f8e8ff4c966df77c6a6ebf45877968f7c5) | Dimension names were a list of two `NULL`s | [0.29.8 (`7edde30`)](https://github.com/Bioconductor/DelayedArray/commit/7edde30ebf5bc602d7e6c9094a25bef2a4eb0b6a) |
| `tenx-coercion/preserve-nan` | [0.31.9 (`5afb60e`)](https://github.com/Bioconductor/DelayedArray/commit/5afb60eaaf583facaebd54a848db704d907d6e2a) | Coercion replaced `NaN` with `0` | [0.31.10 (`1689c0f`)](https://github.com/Bioconductor/DelayedArray/commit/1689c0f9f1deb6cff0e64067a37412d4f6d7b330) |

To repeat a historical failure, install the linked revision in an
isolated library with its dependencies and start a fresh R session with
that library first. Run the setup, case and generation chunks above, then
use the chunk below in place of the current-dependency check. Set `id`
to the case from the table and compare the printed diagnostic to that
row. To replay in a later session, use a persistent `work` directory in
the setup and keep it together with the versioned library. Replay
restores the case's seed and checks the source revision. The evidence
records dependency versions for comparison.

```{r historical-replay, eval=FALSE}
id <- "tenx-coercion/preserve-nan"
failed <- biocroxytest::run_test_plan(pkg, ids = id, seed = 42L)
stopifnot(identical(failed$cases$status, "failed"))
cat(failed$cases$detail, "\n")

record <- file.path(work, "failure.rds")
biocroxytest::write_test_replay(failed, id, record)
replayed <- biocroxytest::replay_test_case(record, path = pkg)
stopifnot(isTRUE(replayed$comparison$same_failure))
```

Both historical failures replayed with matching signatures. To check a
fix, run `run_test_plan(pkg, ids = id)` in the fixed library and pass its
report to `check_test_plan(report, required = id)`. The reduction here
was manual. The named tests reuse the same small inputs and assertions
across versions and distinguish an incorrect result from a case that
could not run.

```{r cleanup}
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE, expand = FALSE)
```
